record.abstract: In vehicular integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks, each service-provider vehicle uses a limited power budget to serve multiple sensing targets and communication receivers. Maximizing the communication sum-rate subject to sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints is nonconvex, and iterative optimization is costly to rerun for every network layout. This paper proposes a graph neural network (GNN)-based power allocation algorithm, termed GNN-ISAC. Concretely, GNN-ISAC addresses the aforementioned problem by considering two distinct edge types in the graph representation, one capturing the inter-provider interference, the other representing the intra-provider power-budget sharing. GNN-ISAC is trained without labels using a sensing-penalized sum-rate loss. We also adapt the weighted mean-square error minimization (WMMSE) algorithm to this problem by introducing a sensing-power reservation step. Simulation results show that GNN-ISAC achieves communication sum-rates close to WMMSE with low sensing-link violation rates and much less computation. It also outperforms an existing heterogeneous GNN and a channel-blind baseline, and generalizes to larger networks without retraining.

record.abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) model signals as continuous functions from coordinates to values, but their performance depends strongly on how spectral capacity is allocated. Yet most Quantum INR (QINR) architectures treat spectral components as independent outputs of separate quantum blocks. We introduce the Spectral Quantum Memory Model (SQMM), a memory coupled quantum INR in which sequential hybrid data reuploading layers (bands) communicate through a shared coherent quantum memory register. Each band reads the memory, computes on its own coordinate upload, and writes part of its state back, so later bands can build on the computation of earlier ones. When memory read and write layers are input independent, we prove that the memory state forms an operator valued Fourier series whose support is contained in the Minkowski sum of the initial memory spectrum and the local band spectra. Downstream bands then condition their Fourier coefficients on the spectral content stored by earlier bands, and the memory coupling creates no new primitive frequencies. This theory motivates a spectral memory alignment loss that encourages memory to encode the spectrum expressed by the deployed prefix of the model. Across audio and image reconstruction benchmarks, SQMM improves over compact QINR and INR baselines.

record.abstract: Object detection research remains constrained by high annotation costs and the closed-set assumptions of supervised models, limiting scalability to novel categories. Our method autonomously generates segmentation proposals, assigns semantic labels through multimodal reasoning, and iteratively improves both localization and classification using a lightweight open-set detector. This modular pipeline enables adaptation to completely unseen object classes and domains without any human-provided target-dataset annotations, while maintaining compatibility with existing detection architectures. record.abstract: Digital Twins are evolving from passive virtual representations into closed-loop systems that continuously synchronize with physical assets and drive real-time decisions. Yet predictive modeling, machine learning (ML), uncertainty quantification (UQ), and decision-making have been studied as separate capabilities, leaving limited understanding of their integration and maintenance during online operation. This narrative review, scoped by the functional requirements of real-time decision-making rather than by Digital Twin terminology alone, examines how such decisions are generated and sustained in engineering Digital Twins. We first examine foundational decision-making architectures and representative engineering applications, followed by methods that address their limitations across the decision loop. We identify optimization-based, policy-based, and knowledge-based approaches as the major pathways from virtual representation to action. Across them, ML plays three roles in decision-making: enabling efficient surrogate modeling, transforming heterogeneous physical feedback into decision-relevant information, and accelerating or directly generating decisions. UQ supports uncertainty-aware decisions and model adaptation, while continual validation, drift detection, and adaptation help maintain reliable operation as the physical system evolves. Together, these findings underscore the need for a shift from a model-centric to a system-centric perspective on Digital Twins, where its performance depends on the interactions with sensing, state estimation, computation, decision-making, and adaptation rather than on their standalone performance. Therefore, future research should shift from isolated algorithm development toward system-level co-design, scalable decision-making, and approaches to design, and data-efficient continual adaptation and validation for AI-enabled autonomous systems.

record.abstract: Financial fraud screening operates under fixed investigation capacity, so overall discrimination may not indicate how many fraudulent transactions reach reviewers. Budget and review-window analyses show that the marginal value of explicit rule gating depends on the allocation policy and validation-selected coefficients. record.abstract: The tumour suppressor p53, encoded by TP53, is among the most frequently altered genes in human cancer yet it remains a challenging therapeutic target. Its role as a transcription factor, the absence of a conventional catalytic pocket and the diversity of oncogenic mutations have complicated the development of p53 directed small molecules. Natural products offer a chemically diverse source of candidate scaffolds that may influence wild-type or mutant p53. Carissa macrocarpa (Natal plum) an edible member of the Apocynaceae family, contains anthocyanins, flavonoids and phenolic acids, but its possible mechanisms of action remain incompletely characterised. This review brings together evidence on four related topics: the phytochemistry and ethnopharmacology of Carissa p53 structure biology and mutation patterns therapeutic approaches to p53 modulation, including natural-product-derived compounds; and the strengths and limitations of molecular docking, drug-likeness rules and in silico absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicity (ADMET) prediction. Particular consideration is given to the trade-off between predicted binding and oral developability, the uncertainty of docking scores, and formulation approaches that may improve exposure to polyphenolic compounds. Overall, docking and ADMET workflows are most appropriately used to priorities hypotheses for testing not to establish anticancer activity. A staged validation framework is proposed to guide the assessment of computationally prioritised C. macrocarpa phytochemicals against wild-type and mutant p53.

record.abstract: To track state of health (SOH), second-life potential and design warranties, it is necessary to accurately characterise lithium-ion battery capacity degradation. This paper compares the methodological approaches used for regression models of capacity fade, using synthetic degradation curves which are built from the structure of the publicly available Oxford Battery Degradation Dataset 1 (OBDD1) of eight 740 mAh cells discharged using an ARTEMIS urban drive-cycle at 40 °C, with each degradation profile sampled every 100 cycles. The quantitative results provided are thus illustrative, whereas the qualitative conclusions made on the problem of model selection are robust and extend to the real data. Linear, quadratic and cubic polynomials are compared to describe the capacity-versus-cycle trajectory and compared to Gaussian process regression (GPR) for prediction of end of life (EOL, 80% SOH). The quadratic model fits the dominant fade (R² ≈ 0.97), the cubic model improves the fit with the “knee” in the later life of the battery (R² ≈ 0.99), and GPR has the lowest point error (RMSE ≈ 2 mAh), but the gain over the cubic polynomial is low in absolute terms (about 0.3% of nominal capacity), and GPR's primary benefit is the well-calibrated uncertainty rather than point accuracy. From the early-life extrapolation experiment, it can be observed that the remaining useful life is consistently overestimated by low-order polynomials and thus the motivation of using uncertainty-aware approaches. The entire pipeline is made available as reproducible code, to enable direct substitution of real measurements.

record.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-supported telemedicine may extend clinical expertise to rural communities, yet its benefits can be offset by unequal connectivity, digital literacy, data representation, and institutional readiness. This study examined the efficacy and health-equity implications of AI-powered telemedicine in post-pandemic rural Indonesia. A qualitative-dominant, convergent mixed-methods secondary study integrated reflexive thematic analysis of peer-reviewed qualitative evidence and Indonesian policy documents with descriptive synthesis of verified national and clinical datasets. Evidence included 2023 national internet statistics, a 63,012-person chronic-disease survey, a 311-patient rheumatology survey, and a 15-interview qualitative study. Telemedicine was most effective for stable follow-up, medication management, specialist access, and travel-cost avoidance, but was less reliable for first diagnosis, unstable disease, and examination-dependent care. Rural internet use (59.33%) remained 17.47 percentage points below urban use (76.80%). Among people with hypertension and/or diabetes, 98.0% reported no telemedicine use, indicating a substantial implementation gap. Four integrated themes emerged: conditional clinical efficacy, redistributed rather than eliminated access burdens, algorithmic amplification of structural disadvantage, and the necessity of human-mediated hybrid care. Conclusion: AI-powered telemedicine is neither inherently equalizing nor intrinsically exclusionary. Its equity effect depends on assisted access, low-bandwidth design, representative validation, clinician oversight, interoperability, and disaggregated monitoring.

record.abstract: Looped transformers apply a shared block several times per token to improve accuracy without adding parameters. For models such as Ouro that keep a separate key-value (KV) cache per loop, cache memory limits the batch size that amortizes repeated weight reads. Uniform-bit quantization and fixed rules per loop do not allocate precision according to each layer's sensitivity in each loop. Measurements on Ouro show that quantization sensitivity varies across (loop, layer) cells, and the sum of individual cell damages approximates the overall output damage. Sharing damage also varies by cell, with later loops generally tolerating sharing better. Skipping low-attention values to save reads produces errors that compound across loops. LoopKV uses a one-time offline profile to choose 4-bit storage, 2-bit storage or reuse of the final loop's KV for each cell. The planner minimizes reads under budgets for predicted damage and storage. During decoding, each loop reads the high 2 bits of each 4-bit value and fetches the low bits only where its own attention weights require 4-bit precision. A single fused kernel in vLLM executes the plan. Serving Ouro-1.4B on one RTX PRO 6000, the memory-optimized LoopKV-M plan stores 35% less KV than uniform 4-bit quantization (KIVI-4) on the same fused kernel and CUDA graph. It sustains 1.7-2.2x KIVI-4's goodput under a latency service-level objective with a 16K-token maximum length. None of its averages on six public benchmarks falls significantly below BF16's.

record.abstract: The integration of advanced materials and intelligent technologies is transforming sustainable engineering by enabling resource-efficient manufacturing, adaptive systems, real-time monitoring, and improved human–machine interaction. Conventional engineering approaches often rely on resource-intensive materials, energy-consuming processes, and limited monitoring capabilities, creating environmental and operational challenges throughout product life cycles. Advanced materials, including conductive polymers, nanofibers, stimuli-responsive polymers, shape-memory materials, photovoltaic fibers, and flexible electronic structures, offer opportunities to address these challenges through multifunctionality, lightweight design, and improved system adaptability. Concurrently, intelligent technologies, such as embedded sensors, digital monitoring systems, data-driven decision support, and connected wearable devices, support more efficient resource utilization and condition-based operation. Smart textiles provide a particularly relevant example because they combine material innovation with sensing, communication, energy harvesting, and user-oriented functionality. Applications in healthcare, industrial safety, energy management, environmental monitoring, and engineering education demonstrate the interdisciplinary potential of these technologies. However, their sustainable implementation requires careful consideration of material toxicity, manufacturing energy, durability, washability, electronic waste, recyclability, data privacy, and economic accessibility. This paper presents a literature-based technical review of advanced materials and intelligent technologies for sustainable engineering applications. It examines material characteristics, technological integration, application domains, environmental considerations, and implementation barriers. It also discusses life-cycle assessment, circular product design, sustainability-oriented engineering education, and challenge-based learning as complementary strategies for responsible innovation. The review indicates that technological performance alone is insufficient to establish sustainability; environmental integrity, human well-being, economic feasibility, and end-of-life management must be considered together. An integrated framework combining sustainable material selection, intelligent system design, lifecycle evaluation, and interdisciplinary education is proposed to guide future research and engineering practice.

record.abstract: The objective of this study to propose a methodology to examine nanofluids flow enhanced thermal conductivity and heat transfer behaviour. The study aims to depict the optimised parameter values at which enhanced thermal conductivity of nanofluids results in more efficient cooling. To achieve this, mixed convection nanofluid (Cu-water) flow over a shrinking sheet under radiative effects is investigated numerically using finite element method (FEM). The analysis incorporates key parameters such as the suction, thermal conductivity, radiation and mixed convection which govern the flow and heat transfer characteristics. The numerical investigation depicts that suction is the most dominant factor which helps to reduce the boundary layer thickness and enhance heat transfer. Radiative effects lead to a thicker thermal boundary layer that consequently reduces the heat transfer rate. The mixed convection parameter also contributes to higher heat transfer rate, simultaneously increasing the skin friction. Corresponding diagrams are plotted to illustrate the outcomes. Results show that the nanofluid model developed in this work exhibits higher Nusselt number as compared to the base microfluid model, confirming improved heat transfer. Also, results obtained statistically by Response Surface Methodology (RSM) using MATLAB® are investigated for optimised value of parameters. The results from the RSM model show a strong positive correlation with our numerical FEM results. The RSM-ANOVA optimisation reveals a strong correlation, giving accuracy of 0.975, highlighting the roles of suction and radiative heat transfer in determining thermal behaviour. This study provides insights for effective thermal management in thin-film manufacturing processes.

record.abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability provides certified backward reachable tubes (BRTs) for safety-critical robotic systems, but the level-set computation scales exponentially in the state dimension and has historically been performed offline. As autonomy stacks (ADAS/AV, humanoid robotics, and vision-language-action models) increasingly rely on black-box, probabilistic policies, a deterministic safety layer with formal guarantees is an essential complement. We present a CUDA implementation of the canonical WENO5 + TVD-RK3 + Lax-Friedrichs level-set Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs solver for 2D, 3D, and 4D dynamics that is fast enough to run inside a robot's control loop. In 32-bit floating point (FP32) on a single workstation GPU (NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada), it computes the 3D Air3D BRT at 112 Hz, a 4D pursuit-evasion BRT at 61 Hz, and a 2D wind-affected drifter BRT at 74-147 Hz, 5.9-17.5x faster than the JAX reference hj_reachability at matched precision and 1.7-16x faster than a torch.compile reimplementation of the same scheme. record.abstract: Underwater acoustic communication faces challenges such as limited available bandwidth and complex channel environments, which impose demanding requirements on efficient image transmission and reliable reconstruction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a generative image communication framework based on cross-modal semantic successive refinement. At the transmitter, text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and visual side information compressed by residual vector quantization are transmitted. record.abstract: Existing generative model-based approaches to linear inverse problems typically use the acquired noisy measurement to condition or guide sampling in the image domain. In this work, we introduce Dual Flow, a novel joint flow model for solving linear inverse problems by jointly estimating the clean image and its corresponding noise-free measurement from the observation. Specifically, Dual Flow formulates image reconstruction and measurement denoising as a coupled estimation problem, using coupled flows in the image and measurement domains. The acquired noisy measurement $\mathbf{y}_0$ is used only to initialize the measurement state; thereafter, the image and measurement states are jointly updated based on their current values. By construction, the final image and measurement estimates are guaranteed to satisfy the underlying forward model. We derive the sampling updates for the joint flow and show that they are governed by the conditional mean of the clean image given the current joint state. We further derive a closed-form expression for a sufficient statistic of the joint state and show that the required conditional mean can be obtained by solving an image-domain Gaussian denoising problem involving operator-dependent, correlated noise. We train a velocity-prediction network using this formulation to estimate the conditional mean from the derived sufficient statistic. Dual Flow requires no hyperparameter tuning beyond selecting the number of inference steps and achieves substantially shorter reconstruction times than competing methods. Extensive experiments across various linear inverse problems and image datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both distortion metrics and perceptual quality. Additional analyses assess robustness to model mismatch, as well as the ability to generate diverse plausible reconstructions and characterize reconstruction uncertainty.

record.abstract: Promptable perception, from GroundingDINO to Rex-Omni, puts one model behind one prompt interface and returns coordinates for any localisation task. record.abstract: Causal set theory permits changes of spatial topology without the metric degeneracy that forbids them in continuum Lorentzian gravity. In four dimensions such changes enter the gravitational action only through the Gauss--Bonnet term, which is the Euler density. We show that the Euler density of a discrete space is exact, local and combinatorial: it sums to the Euler characteristic at any resolution and is supported on topological defects. The Gauss--Bonnet term of a causal set is therefore fixed rather than postulated. Because it is linear in the number of elements, which is the four-volume, it acts as a cosmological constant. Its coefficient follows without forming any functional derivative, so the known obstruction in the continuum does not arise. The everpresent cosmological constant of causal set theory assumes that the mean topological charge vanishes. We show that it does not. The species of opposite sign solves the field equations only if a positive cosmological constant is already present, and, being simply connected, it cannot carry the axion charge that supports the other species. Only one sign survives, and the sign of the cosmological term is derived rather than assumed. We recover the surviving transition from the causal order alone in every simulated sprinkling. The action of the corresponding axion wormhole then fixes the magnitude. The observed value requires an axion decay constant near the grand unification scale, and this result is insensitive to the one-loop prefactor and to the Gauss--Bonnet coupling.

record.abstract: Causal questions often arise in systems that evolve in continuous time. While instrumental variable (IV) methods provide a principled approach to identify causal effects in static or discrete-time settings, even in the presence of unobserved confounding, they do not yet extend to continuous-time dynamics. In this work, we develop an IV framework for stationary continuous-time stochastic processes parameterized by stochastic differential equations (SDE), where the instrument itself takes the form of a stochastic process. We encode the structural sparsity and causal effects directly at the infinitesimal level of the drift, and contrast these assumptions with the IV assumptions on the discretized version of the same process. Based on these structural assumptions, we derive moment restrictions using path-valued instruments. We show how these restrictions simplify for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes and present an identification condition together with a corresponding consistent estimation method. Finally, we extend our estimation framework to nonlinear causal effects by expressing the path-based moment restrictions leveraging the signature kernel. Empirically, our method recovers causal effects in confounded continuous-time systems where maximum-likelihood-based estimation and discrete-time IV methods are systematically biased.

record.abstract: Environment division multiple access (EDMA) has recently emerged as a promising multiple-access paradigm by exploiting the wireless propagation environment for user separation, while physical-layer security, including secrecy and covert communication, is becoming increasingly important for protecting confidential information and user privacy. record.abstract: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), the same base-station array beamforms toward users and estimates their angle of arrival (AoA). In this paper, we study how element-level gain, phase, and position errors affect both functions of a beam-scanning uniform linear array. Any array produces a correlation peak at the true angle, of finite height and width, surrounded by sidelobes. Impairments shift this peak, make it lower and wider, and raise the sidelobes relative to it. A single decomposition explains these three effects: the gain-weighted least-squares fit of the per-antenna phase errors splits them into a tilt, which shifts the peak, and a residual, whose power is taken from the peak and redistributed over the sidelobes according to its spatial spectrum. A beam steered toward the strongest direction suffers from the lower peak only, whereas the AoA estimate suffers from its shift even without noise, and also from the lowering and sidelobes with noise. The worst cases for the two ISAC functions are thus nearly disjoint, and we characterize both: the worst case for beamforming leaves the AoA estimate unbiased, and the worst case for localization loses little beamforming gain. The worst case for localization is a single defect at the junction between two subarrays, and its error, relative to the main-lobe width, does not decrease with the number of antennas. We also characterize random impairments and the effect of noise. In practical terms, our analysis shows that the calibration of a dual-function array must be assessed with respect to both functions.

record.abstract: In networked integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), a base station (BS) performing sensing using its own downlink signals is subject to interference from the downlink transmissions of neighboring BSs. record.abstract: Semantic information can enrich the identifiers and structured fields used by recommender systems. Semantic tokenization provides a structured representation of this information by converting LLM-derived user profiles into discrete tokens. In the common two-stage pipeline, the tokenizer is trained before the recommender. Its token assignments are then treated as fixed input features during recommendation training. As a result, the downstream recommender can learn how to use the assigned indices, but it cannot revise the semantic partition that produced them. Making this partition task-aware is difficult because nearest-code assignment is discrete, and unconstrained adaptation may also distort the geometry learned during pretraining. Moreover, a fixed token depth exposes the same semantic resolution to every interaction. We thus propose OptST (Optimizing Semantic Tokenization), which makes a pretrained tokenizer responsive to downstream recommendation. To revise token assignments without directly updating the pretrained encoder or base codebooks, OptST learns a low-rank deformation whose drift is limited by an anchor regularizer. Recommendation supervision reaches this transformation through a straight-through estimator, while prediction retains hard nearest-code assignments. Beyond adapting the assignments themselves, OptST selects an interaction-conditioned prefix to control how much residual detail is exposed to the recommender. Experiments on four public datasets show that OptST achieves the highest AUC among conventional and LLM-enhanced baselines. Its improvements also persist across different recommendation backbones. These results establish task-aware semantic tokenization as an effective interface between LLM-derived profiles and downstream recommendation models.

record.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human behavior, their operational validity is typically assessed through accuracy alone, implicitly treating human behavior as deterministic. record.abstract: Predicting stock returns requires modeling persistent company relations and time-varying market signals. record.abstract: Planning has been identified as an important factor for improved code generation with Large Language Models (LLMs). However, the interaction between planning capability and coding capability remains largely underexplored, especially when the two capabilities are from different LLMs. In this paper, we conduct the first comprehensive empirical study of planning-coding interaction in LLM-based code generation, where planning and coding are assigned to different LLMs (i.e., planning-coding separation). Specifically, we explore different planner-coder combinations to investigate the effectiveness for coders to utilize planning information from various planners and the impact of further training of coders on planner-coder combinations. Our results demonstrate that almost all planner-coder combinations are as competitive as using the same LLM for planning and coding, and the combination of a stronger planner and a stronger coder typically achieves improved effectiveness. Furthermore, using a large model as the planner paired with a much smaller model as the coder can sometimes be as competitive as using the large model as both the planner and the coder, and further training of the coder can typically boost various planner-coder combinations. These findings provide empirical evidence that planning and coding can be separated to a considerable extent in LLM-based code generation, which may offer a more flexible way to construct code-generation systems.

record.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is increasingly used in settings where pairwise preferences coexist with pointwise criteria such as response length, answer correctness, or safety scores. When the two disagree, standard DPO treats pairs whose preferred output scores worse on the pointwise criterion (conflict pairs) in the same way as the remaining (matching) pairs. We characterize a systematic failure mode, constraint drift: for sufficiently small updates, conflict pairs tend to increase constraint cost while matching pairs tend to repair it, and the net change depends on their balance. This balance yields a closed-form pre-alignment diagnostic, $ρ^{*}_{\mathrm{eq}}$, computable from dataset statistics, that indicates whether a dataset is self-correcting or requires intervention. Building on this diagnostic, we propose Conflict-aware DPO (CoDPO), which down-weights conflict pairs with a strength set from $ρ^{*}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ rather than tuned, and adds an adaptive margin shift that addresses residual drift during training. Empirically, drift grows monotonically with conflict exposure on the conflict-dominated domains, and the intervention decision given by $ρ^{*}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ matches the observed drift on every domain, including one that it identifies as self-correcting. On all four domains of the main comparison, CoDPO reduces drift while largely preserving the preference learning of vanilla DPO. Compared with hard filtering and recent constrained and multi-objective baselines, CoDPO also achieves a more favorable drift-preference trade-off.

record.abstract: Collaborative-filtering (CF) scores provide graded, personalized rewards for training large language model (LLM) recommenders through reinforcement learning. However, these rewards can cause exposure collapse: even though the CF model itself produces diverse top recommendations across users, an LLM optimized with its rewards concentrates on fewer items. We decompose each score into an item-mean component, the item's average CF score across user histories, and a residual component, the current user's score deviation from the average. Through controlled interventions, we identify the item-mean component as a contributor to exposure collapse. Accordingly, we propose two reward corrections: per-item centering removes each item's estimated mean score, while per-item standardization further rescales the residual using its estimated standard deviation. Experiments on two datasets with two identifier schemes show that both corrections substantially improve catalog coverage and exposure evenness. Compared with training on the uncorrected CF reward, our corrections increase the number of distinct items ranked first across users by up to $9.8\times$, while maintaining comparable ranking accuracy. record.abstract: Symmetry governs the organization of physical structures, while symmetry breaking reveals their transformations. In geometric deep learning, symmetry imposes rank constraints on equivariant representations, limiting the expressive capacity of equivariant graph neural networks (GNNs). Here we show that these constraints can instead be exploited: the singular-value spectra of equivariant representations provide a unified fingerprint of structural symmetry. We introduce spectral symmetry fingerprints (SymFP), which enable discrete point-group identification through rank-template matching and continuous symmetry analysis by quantifying spectral energy beyond target rank constraints. SymFP is orientation invariant and architecture agnostic, enabling a parameter-free GNN implementation. Its spectra can be reused across multiple target groups, and the resulting leakage scores satisfy subgroup monotonicity. Across synthetic structures, molecules, coordination complexes and large biological assemblies, SymFP accurately identifies point groups, tracks controlled symmetry breaking and reveals local and degree-resolved symmetry changes that can be obscured by global geometric measures. These results establish the spectral structure of equivariant representations as a general framework for characterizing symmetry across physical systems.

record.abstract: Modular multilevel converter (MMC) has become an attractive technology for high-power electronics applications thanks to its high energy efficiency, high power rating, high modularity, flexible scalability, and superior output waveform quality. It has attracted considerable research attention, and numerous submodule (SM) variants have been developed for different objectives. Among them, the half-bridge SM (HBSM) is the most widely adopted thanks to its simplicity, but it cannot interrupt DC-side short-circuit currents. Various SM topologies with fault-blocking capability have been proposed. These SM topologies contain additional switches and passive components compared to the HBSM, leading to higher capital and operating costs. Aiming at these issue, an SM topology capable to block DC-side fault-currents with a reduced component count is proposed in this paper. The proposed SM includes two variants, one employs only two fully-controlled switches. An operation and control scheme for the proposed SM are also developed and presented in the paper. The functionality of the proposed SM is validated by experiment, and the value of the SM is demonstrated through a test simulation for an high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) transmission system.

record.abstract: Object rearrangement in cluttered tabletop scenes is challenging, especially in wide workspaces where dual-arm systems improve coverage and efficiency. Limited free space often necessitates buffering, while objects near or across the shared reachability region of the manipulators must be transferred under careful coordination to avoid inter-arm collisions. Conventional inter-arm transfer typically relies on a fixed handoff configuration, which constrains where and how objects are exchanged, enforces spatiotemporal synchronization of the arms, and reduces flexibility in dense layouts. This paper presents a dual-arm rearrangement framework that combines movable stacking with Gap-Aware Push Transfer for asynchronous cross-boundary exchange. The method scans the shared boundary to identify collision-free transfer gaps, places an object near a selected crossing point, and then pushes it into the receiving workspace without requiring simultaneous interaction between the two arms. A joint Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-based planner coordinates both manipulators while reasoning over buffering and transfer decisions, and execution cost is used after planning to assess the resulting plan. Experiments show that the proposed method shortens joint execution sequences and becomes increasingly advantageous over a fixed handoff baseline as scene density increases, achieving lower execution cost in denser scenes while remaining competitive in lighter ones.

record.abstract: We propose an altermagnetism-induced route to a two-dimensional higher-order topological Dirac semimetal in a trilayer nonsymmorphic Dirac system. Interlayer hybridization preserves the nonsymmorphic bulk Dirac crossings and generates helical edge states in the trilayer phase. Introducing outer-layer $d$-wave altermagnetic order gaps the helical edge states, while only the symmetry-protected Dirac crossing at high-symmetry point $M$ remains gapless. The resulting phase hosts a surviving bulk Dirac point, gapped edge spectra, and corner states. An exact layer-space decomposition further reveals that these features arise from the coexistence of a gapless Dirac sector and a gapped $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological sector. Our results establish altermagnetism as an effective mechanism for engineering higher-order topological Dirac semimetals in two-dimensional nonsymmorphic systems.

record.abstract: Position--stiffness regulation of antagonistic variable stiffness actuators (VSAs) involves coupled nonlinear dynamics, parameter uncertainty, and feedback states that are not directly measured. This paper addresses this challenge through a simulation-based workflow that integrates elastic shaping, model verification, and layered nonlinear control. This study builds on a previously developed actuator comprising two crossed four-bar compliant transmission elastic units. Its optimized elastic mapping provides the structural basis, with an ADAMS torque-curve root mean square error (RMSE) of $2.57\,\mathrm{N\!\cdot\!mm}$ against the target. A control-oriented analytical model is implemented in Simulink and compared with the independently executed ADAMS model under matched inputs. The maximum joint-angle RMSE across the tested cases is $4.66\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{rad}$. A layered controller combines extended Kalman filtering for state reconstruction, feedback linearization for nominal decoupling, and adaptive sliding-mode control for residual compensation. At the end of the nominal simulation, the joint-angle error is approximately $3.14\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{rad}$. The stiffness error is $3.07\,\mathrm{N\!\cdot\!mm/rad}$ relative to a target of $50\,\mathrm{N\!\cdot\!mm/rad}$. Parameter-variation and ablation tests assess tracking performance and the effects of the controller modules within the evaluated conditions. The resulting workflow links structural-response modeling, state estimation, and robust control assessment, supporting repeatable comparisons beyond nominal tracking alone.

record.abstract: Background and Aim: Probiotic cultures often lose viability during processing and storage, which limits their use in functional dairy products. This study compared the survival of free and alginate/pullulan-microencapsulated Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG ATCC 53103 (LGG) in soft goat cheese during refrigerated storage and simulated in vitro digestion. Methods: Goat milk was pasteurized at 85 °C for 10 s, inoculated with a commercial starter culture and rennet and then held at 30 °C ±1 for 15 h. The curd was salted with 1% (ww-1) NaCl and stored at 4 °C for 30 d. The LGG was added as free cells or in alginate/pullulan microcapsules and three independently made batches were assessed. Free cells were mixed with trehalose (20% of cell mass) as a cryoprotectant before freeze-drying. Microcapsules were assessed using optical and scanning electron microscopy. A modified two-stage in vitro digestion model was used to investigate bacterial survival during simulated gastrointestinal digestion. Results and Conclusion: Presumptive LGG counts on MRS agar decreased during storage in the two cheeses, but the decrease was smaller in the cheese containing microcapsules. On Day 30, counts were 8.01 ±0.16 log CFU·g-1 for encapsulated cells and 6.22 ±0.05 log CFU·g-1 for free cells, corresponding to losses of 0.61 and 2.39 log units, respectively. The difference between treatments at this time point was significant (adjusted p < 0.05). After the intestinal phase of simulated digestion, counts were 7.96 ±0.06 log CFU·g-1 for encapsulated cells and 6.12 ±0.07 log CFU·g-1 for the free cells. Under the conditions assessed, alginate/pullulan microencapsulation improved the retention of culturable LGG in soft goat cheese during refrigerated storage and simulated gastrointestinal digestion. INTRODUCTION Within the past few decades, consumers have shown increasing interests in functional foods, which may offer health benefits in addition to basic nutrition [1,2]. Probiotic foods are a major group within this category. They contain live microorganisms that confer a health benefit on the host when administered in adequate quantities [3]. Probiotic bacteria have been shown to help maintain the balance of the intestinal microbiota, support immune function and prevent gastrointestinal disorders [3–5]. Dairy products are widely used to deliver probiotic cultures to consumers because they suit these organisms well and are technologically convenient [6–8]. Industrial use of probiotics is limited by two requirements. Enough viable cells must persist through processing and storage and the cells must survive passage through the gastrointestinal tract (GIT) [9–11]. A probiotic product must include enough viable cells until the end of its shelf life. There is, however, no single minimum count that holds for every strain and every health outcome. The quantity the product delivers should match the dose that is shown effective for that particular strain and the intended benefit [9]. In the GIT, viability decreases by low gastric pH, bile salts and digestive enzymes. During processing and storage, it decreases by heating, oxygen exposure, osmotic stress, dehydration and prolonged refrigeration [10–12]. Goat milk is not an inherently poor matrix for probiotic cultures: its nutrient composition may support their survival. Its casein profile and physicochemical characteristics, however, can affect fermentation, curd formation, texture and the viability of individual strains [13–15]. Thus, probiotic survival needs assessment for each strain-matrix combination. Freeze-drying, spray-drying and microencapsulation have been developed to improve probiotic survival. Microencapsulation is generally addressed as the most promising technique. The capsule wall shields cells from adverse conditions and may allow targeted delivery and controlled release in the intestines [16,17]. How well it acts depends on the wall material, encapsulation method, particle size and strain as well as processing and storage conditions [17]. Most current studies use natural biopolymers such as alginate, pectin, chitosan, starch, plant gums and dairy and plant proteins. Prebiotic ingredients, including inulin, fructooligosaccharides, galactooligo-saccharides and resistant starch, can be added to the matrix. Such a formulation should be called synbiotic only if the host microorganisms or the coadministered strain select-ively use the substrate and the combination has been shown to confer a health benefit [18,19]. Goat cheese has been studied as a probiotic carrier because of its nutritional value and its physicochemical composition [13,20]. Studies with free and microen-capsulated strains of Lactobacillus, Lacticaseibacillus and Bifidobacterium show that adding probiotics can change the physicochemical, textural and sensory characteristics of goat cheese. The direction and size of these changes depend on the strain, encapsulation system, cheese formulation and storage conditions [20–22]. In a previous study on goat cheese, microencapsulated probiotics survived refrigerated storage better than that free cells did [21,22]. Lopes et al. [21] detected that microencapsulated L. acidophilus La-05 in spreadable goat Ricotta tolerated simulated gastrointestinal digestion better. A few studies, however, have directly compared free and microen-capsulated L. rhamnosus GG (LGG) in soft goat cheeses. record.abstract: KV cache compression reduces the communication volume of disaggregated large language model serving, but its practical benefit depends not only on compression ratio and model quality, but also on how efficiently the compression pipeline executes. This requirement becomes increasingly important as modern serving systems adopt high-bandwidth interconnects, where inefficient compression can offset a substantial portion of the saved communication time. This paper presents FastKVComp, a high-throughput KV cache compression data path built on top of KVServe. FastKVComp improves compression execution in two complementary ways. First, it fuses the distribution transformation and low-bit quantization stages into a KVaware TileLang kernel, eliminating intermediate tensor materialization and redundant memory accesses. Second, it replaces the original lossless compression backend with an open, extensible, and searchable backend based on LC, enabling high-performance compression operator pipelines. The fused kernel achieves up to 5.9x speedup, while the new lossless backend increases compression throughput from below 90 GB/s to over 500 GB/s. Across the evaluated workloads, FastKVComp reduces job completion time by up to 2.04x. End-to-end evaluation shows that these optimizations allow KV compression to retain meaningful communication benefits under modern high-bandwidth network.

record.abstract: We study the fixed points and stability of a nonlinear operator associated with the three-state SOS model with one-level competing interactions on the binary Cayley tree. We provide an exact characterization of the parameter regions corresponding to one through seven positive fixed points of the associated nonlinear operator. For the physically relevant case in which the competing interaction coincides with the nearest-neighbour interaction, we determine the critical values separating different phase transition regimes and obtain a complete classification of the positive fixed points. We further investigate their local stability by analyzing the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix and classify the fixed points as attracting, repelling, or saddle. The analytical results are complemented by phase portraits illustrating the qualitative dynamics of the nonlinear operator.

record.abstract: Panoptic Scene Graph generation (PSG) requires holistic yet fine-grained reasoning over complex relations among objects. However, current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) applied to PSG suffer from a perception bottleneck: they function as static observers limited by fixed-resolution views. As a result, models often overlook critical relations involving small or peripheral objects and struggle to differentiate ambiguous predicates in complex scenes. To address these limitations, we propose PSGAgent, an agentic framework that enhances visual perception for PSG through a think-act-observe loop. PSGAgent allows MLLMs to dynamically refine their visual perception using two tools: a Region Zoom-In Tool for local exploration of small or boundary relations and a Visual Highlight Tool for relation-focused segmentation that filters out irrelevant contextual noise. To optimize decision-making, we construct a two-stage training pipeline. First, we create a high-quality, error-aware Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (M-CoT) dataset that provides robust supervision for cold-start learning. Then, we design a novel hierarchical reward mechanism integrated with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) to enable strategic and adaptive tool usage. Extensive experiments on the PSG benchmark show that PSGAgent achieves SOTA performance, demonstrating strong capability in both holistic and fine-grained scene understanding.

record.abstract: EVAR has come to be regarded as a major minimally invasive surgery to cure complex aneurysms yet problematic postoperative issues like endoleaks, graft migration, thrombosis, and expansion of the aneurysm sac remain clinical issues. This report suggests an AI-boosted haemodynamic model to predict the occurrence of post-endovascular complications by incorporating patient-specific vascular imaging, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and machine learning in its predictive algorithms. The introduced methodology involves the use of the computed tomography angiography (CTA) information, three-dimensional vascular tree reconstruction and parameters of hemodynamics, which include: the wall shear stress, oscillatory shear index, pressure gradient and blood flow velocity. The methodology incorporates four machine learning algorithms such as: Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Support Vector Machine and Artificial Neural Network, which may help to perform predictive analysis. The experimentally achieved results as an example illustrate that XGBoost reaches the highest classification accuracy (93.6%) and ROC-AUC (0.96). This means that this algorithm can be applied for identification of the risk of postoperative complications. Also, the influence of the wall shear stress and pressure gradient is illustrated with the feature importance analysis. The presented framework is expected to be a promising computation technique to achieve the stratification of risks, postoperative monitoring and medical decision-making in an individual way. Further validation using multicenter clinical data sets should be performed to test the reliability and practicality of this approach in aneurysms treatment.

record.abstract: We study a translation-invariant two-channel Hamiltonian on the two-dimensional lattice Z 2 describing two identical spinless bosons with no direct boson–boson interaction, coupled through an on-site association/dissociation term of strength γ ∈ R to a structureless molecular channel of fixed scalar internal energy E 0 ∈ R. The model is a 2 × 2 block operator matrix; it is translation invariant and admits a fiber decomposition over the total quasi-momentum k ∈ T 2 , whose fibers H γ (k) act on C ⊕ L 2,e (T 2 ). The perturbation distinguishing H γ (k) from the free operator has rank at most two, so the essential spectrum of each fiber is [ϵ min (k), ϵ max (k)], equal to [0, 16] at k = 0, independently of E 0 and γ. For the distinguished fiber H γ (0), we determine the discrete spectrum completely and uniformly in the coupling: when γ = 0, the channels decouple and the only discrete eigenvalue is the bare molecular level E 0 , present exactly when E 0 ∈/ [0, 16]; whereas for every γ ̸= 0 and every E 0 ∈ R, the operator has exactly two simple discrete eigenvalues, one strictly below and one strictly above the two-boson continuum [0, 16]. In two dimensions, the logarithmic singularity of the lattice Green’s function at the spectral edges makes both bound states appear for arbitrarily weak coupling, the binding energies being exponentially small when E 0 lies inside the continuum and only algebraically small (up to a logarithm) when E 0 sits at a band edge. record.abstract: The buccal drug delivery system is a sophisticated and promising method for delivering medications for both local and systemic therapeutic effects via the buccal mucosa, the inner lining of the cheek. It provides an alternative to traditional oral drug delivery by lessening the effects of hepatic first-pass metabolism and gastrointestinal degradation for appropriate medications. This strategy may increase patient compliance, provide regulated medication release, improve drug bioavailability, and give a practical, non-invasive way to administer drugs. The buccal mucosa's morphology and physiology, drug absorption mechanisms, and the contribution of mucoadhesion to better drug delivery and retention are the main topics of this review. The interaction between mucoadhesive formulations and the mucosal surface is explained by a variety of mucoadhesion theories, such as electronic, adsorption, diffusion, wetting, mechanical, and fracture theories. The significance of natural, semisynthetic, and synthetic mucoadhesive polymers in creating successful buccal formulations is also highlighted in the review. The preparation techniques and formulation elements of various dosage forms, including buccal tablets, films, patches, gels, and wafers, are explained. Additionally, the functions of various excipients and permeation enhancers in enhancing drug transport via the buccal mucosa are investigated. Mucoadhesive strength, swelling index, surface pH, drug content, in vitro drug release, ex vivo permeability, stability, and other crucial evaluation parameters are also covered. Recent developments in nanotechnology, fastdissolving films, nanocarriers, and three-dimensional printing have opened up new possibilities for designing patient-friendly dosage forms and enhancing medication delivery efficacy. However, during formulation creation, issues such salivary secretion, mucosal barrier characteristics, limited absorption area, formulation acceptability, and possible irritation must be taken into account. As a whole, The buccal drug delivery system is an important pharmaceutical strategy that may enhance patient convenience, medication bioavailability, and therapeutic efficacy. The creation of buccal drug delivery formulations that are safer, more effective, and clinically useful may be facilitated by more research and technical developments.

record.abstract: Breast cancer is still a leading cause of cancer deaths and morbidity and is biologically heterogeneous, so treatment needs to be informed by the breast cancer type. ERBB2 is a clinically validated onco-driving gene in a subset of breast cancers; it encodes human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2). Antibody targeting of HER2, tyrosine kinase inhibitors and antibody–drug conjugates have enhanced response rates, but there are still significant problems revolving around resistance, treatment-related cardiac effects, cost and access. Although natural products remain a rich source of structurally diverse starting points for drug discovery, the potential of a plant-derived compound is not solely determined by its ability to bind to the target, it also needs to demonstrate absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) properties. This narrative review compiles literature presented in the author's thesis, present HER2-directed treatment, phytochemistry of Araucaria araucana (Monkey Puzzle tree) and computational screening methods. Specific focus is on 17 phytochemicals, including biflavonoids, diterpenoids, flavonoids/flavanols, phenolic acids, a triterpenoid and a sterol. SwissADME, pkCSM and ProTox-3.0 were used to assess drug-likeness, PK behaviour and toxicity, while molecular docking with the wild-type and mutated ERBB2 was performed. Selected diterpenoids of the sample and flavonols, particularly agathic acid, sugiol and kaempferol, are suggested to be worth further study, while the large biflavonoids and rutin might require further studies of oral-exposure limitations. These results are hypothesis generating and not proof of clinical efficacy or safety. Protocol comparator, molecular-dynamics analysis, biochemical and ce/llular assays, measured pharmacokinetics, cardiac-safety testing are all required for validation. Future studies should focus on sustainable sourcing, reference standards and synthetic or semisynthetic approaches, as A. araucana is endangered.

record.abstract: Recent advances in large language models have enabled agentic systems that automate machine learning pipeline construction from minimal user input. However, existing agentic AutoML methods either depend on rigid templates that limit adaptability, target narrow task domains, or rely on free-form code generation that lacks reliability guarantees, leaving intermediate errors to propagate silently and degrade the final model. We present EvoML, an agentic framework for end-to-end ML pipeline synthesis built on expert-grounded skills that evolve across runs, executed through a validation-gated harness. The framework decomposes pipeline construction into four phases coordinated by three agents: an Orchestrator that enforces validation gates, advancing each phase only when its outputs pass structural, execution, and semantic checks, which precludes error propagation and keeps every artifact auditable; an Executor that runs expert-grounded skills, grounded in the nnU-Net workflow and pairing reusable templates with online adaptation; and a Curator that performs post-run evolution, consolidating the scripts and guidance recovered during a run into the skill library so it improves across datasets. We evaluate EvoML on eight datasets spanning six sophisticated, real-world ML task types, against agentic AutoML systems and command-line coding tools. EvoML achieves full automation and the best final model quality on all eight, spanning segmentation (up to 0.94 Dice), classification (0.99 accuracy), reconstruction (0.95 SSIM), and denoising (0.79 normalized PSNR), while transferring to broader ML tasks.

record.abstract: Generative AI tools have become part of how students study physics, yet unstructured use may reduce students' opportunities to work through problems independently. The Physics AI-Replication (P-A.I.R.) framework structures AI use as a four-step cycle: students identify a challenging problem, obtain an AI-generated explanation and solution, request similar practice problems, and solve them independently before reviewing the AI's solutions. We evaluated P-A.I.R. in 11 algebra- and calculus-based introductory physics sections at four U.S. institutions using a common end-of-semester survey. Most students reported improved conceptual understanding (90.9\%) and found the replicated practice problems helpful (97.7\%), and these two ratings were strongly associated ($r_s = 0.58$). Perceptions of both components, as well as post-engagement confidence ($μ= 7.18$ on a 1-10 scale), were consistent across institutions. Post-engagement confidence was associated with perceived improvement in conceptual understanding ($r_s = 0.37$) and the helpfulness of replicated practice ($r_s = 0.35$), but not with how often students used AI ($r_s = 0.02$) or with self-reported GPA ($r_s = 0.13$). Thematic analysis of open-ended responses showed that students valued AI primarily for conceptual clarification and structured problem solving (63.0\%), while their main concerns were AI accuracy (34.2\%) and the need for explanations that guide rather than simply provide answers (29.7\%). These findings suggest that how students engage with AI matters more than how often they use it, and that frameworks sequencing AI assistance with independent problem solving offer a practical, transferable approach for physics instruction.

record.abstract: Reticulate processes such as hybridization, introgression, and horizontal gene transfer cannot be fully represented by a bifurcating tree. record.abstract: Tissue injury initiates a complex, multicellular programme whose outcome i.e. functional repair or irreversible fibrosis, is determined by the coordinated activity of the stroma-vascular compartment (SVC). This network of resident fibroblasts, vascular mural cells, endothelial cells and immune populations acts as a gatekeeper of tissue integrity. Following ischaemia, trauma, or mechanical damage, extracellular danger signals are sensed by pattern-recognition receptors and transduced into cell type-specific metabolic and mechanical responses. An initial inflammatory wave clears cellular debris, after which endothelial sprouting and matrix deposition proceed toward scar maturation; a collagen-rich structure whose geometry ultimately governs future perfusion. Epigenetic reprogramming and metabolic rewiring enforce each of these transitions while simultaneously imprinting a memory that skews subsequent responses in the context of ageing, diabetes, chronic inflammation or clonal haematopoiesis. Targeting the SVC, rather than the parenchyma alone, now underpins therapeutic strategies spanning precision senolytics, engineered stromal cell grafts, and biomechanically instructive scaffolds.

record.abstract: Background and Aim: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health concern affecting humans, animals, and the environment. Although surveillance has traditionally focused on healthcare settings and livestock, wildlife is increasingly recognized as a potential reservoir, carrier, and indicator of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria and resistance genes. This review examines the ecological factors, movement patterns, and transmission pathways influencing AMR in wildlife, with particular emphasis on potential spillover to humans and domestic animals. Wildlife can acquire resistant microorganisms through contaminated water, soil, food, agricultural runoff, wastewater, and interactions with humans and livestock. Habitat fragmentation, urbanization, agricultural expansion, feeding behavior, and predator–prey relationships further influence exposure and opportunities for bacterial transmission. Local movements and long-distance migration may contribute to the geographical dissemination of resistant bacteria and resistance genes between ecosystems. Evidence from different wildlife populations has identified extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli in migratory birds, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in wild mammals, and fluoroquinolone-resistant bacteria in primates inhabiting areas with frequent human contact. Marine and aquatic wildlife may also contribute to AMR circulation through exposure to wastewater, pharmaceutical residues, and other environmental contaminants. Horizontal gene transfer involving plasmids, integrons, and transposons further contribute to the persistence and dissemination of resistance genes within microbial communities. Humans may be exposed through direct contact, wildlife handling, hunting, and indirect exposure to contaminated water, soil, and food. However, detecting resistant bacteria in wildlife does not necessarily establish the direction or occurrence of transmission to humans. Key challenges include limited wildlife surveillance, inconsistent sampling methods, insufficient ecological data, and difficulty identifying transmission sources. Integrating wildlife monitoring with genomic analysis, environmental surveillance, and animal movement studies could improve understanding of AMR distribution and transmission risks. A coordinated One Health approach involving human health, veterinary, environmental, and wildlife sectors is essential to better characterize potential transmission pathways, strengthen surveillance, and develop effective strategies to reduce AMR spread across interconnected ecosystems. To improve problem solving, most frontier LLMs adopt an MoE architecture, pushing model sizes into the trillion-parameter regime. While cloud services have dominated large-scale LLM inference, cost and security concerns drive demand for on-premises deployment. record.abstract: Harnesses for large language models have converged on a single-threaded shape: one agent, one history, one machine, one sitting. That shape fails work that spans many agents, outlives any one model call, or waits on systems that are not agents. We describe the Agent Board, the coordination substrate in the Corvic harness. The board is a durable, shared table of semi-semantic tasks: a few exact fields the system routes on, and a free-form body that only language models read. Agents post tasks, watch tasks, and block on them, ending their turn and holding no process until a matching post wakes them. A system agent, the Board Keeper, acts as the interrupt handler for the board: it carries events from non-agent parts of the harness onto the board, matches them to waiting tasks by reading their prose, and allocates new agents for tasks that name a kind of agent rather than an instance. Loadable coordination policy kernels give statuses and roles meaning for a given pattern of work, without the board enforcing them. The design mirrors the kanban board a human team puts on a wall. We argue it is what persistent agent products such as Meta Muse, OpenAI dots and SpaceXAI Grok Bot need once an agent must wait, hand off work, or work with agents from another vendor. We view the board as an operating-system scheduler for agents and state where the analogy breaks. We separate what the mechanism guarantees from what it leaves to convention, and report a trace from a live board and three small simulated pilots. In the pilots, the wait cost of the board was flat in wait length while naive polling grew about 165-fold, but a plain external watcher was cheaper than the board. record.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often generate responses longer than necessary, increasing inference latency and computational cost. While prompting can encourage conciseness, controlling output length without compromising response completeness remains challenging. Aggressive early stopping can reduce generation costs but risks terminating responses prematurely. We introduce MinimalLM, a training-free framework for reliable verbosity control that combines uncertainty-aware, length-dependent stop-token adjustment with structural completeness guardrails. MinimalLM separates the decision of when to stop from whether stopping is structurally appropriate, coordinating response-level instructions, decoding-time intervention, and completion checks without modifying model parameters or requiring auxiliary models. We evaluate MinimalLM across three open-source LLMs and 330 questions, producing 5,940 responses across baseline and ablation configurations. MinimalLM reduces generated tokens by 47.6%, accelerates individual responses by 19-68%, and eliminates structurally truncated outputs in the primary evaluation. Despite substantial token savings, it achieves an average quality score of 8.04/10, compared with 8.42/10 for unmodified models and 6.46/10 for length-matched truncation. Evaluations across diverse subject domains (such as healthcare, programming, law, and science) demonstrate robust efficiency gains, while ablations establish the complementary roles of decoding control and completeness constraints. Our findings highlight that efficient generation requires more than producing fewer tokens: it requires controlling when generation ends while preserving response integrity. MinimalLM offers a lightweight, training-free approach toward this goal.

record.abstract: Adrenal gland-induced hypertension results from underlying adrenal gland disorders including Conn's syndrome, Cushing's syndrome, and Pheochromocytoma. Due to the limitations of existing pharmaceutical and surgical treatment methods, minimally invasive treatment options like microwave ablation (MWA) have received significant attention for treating adrenal gland disorders. A precise comprehension of the dielectric properties of human adrenal glands will help to tailor energy delivery for MWA therapy, thus offering the potential to optimise treatments and minimise damage to surrounding tissues. This study reports the ex vivo dielectric properties of human adrenal glands, including the cortex, medulla, capsule, and tumours, based on the data obtained from four patients (diagnosed with Conn's syndrome, Cushing's syndrome, and Pheochromocytoma) who underwent unilateral adrenalectomy at the University Hospital Galway, Ireland. An open-ended coaxial probe measurement technique was used to measure the dielectric properties for a frequency range of 0.5-8.5 GHz. The dielectric properties were fitted using a two-pole Debye model, and a weighted least squares method was employed to optimise the model parameters. Moreover, the dielectric properties of adrenal tissues and tumours were compared across frequencies commonly used in MWA, including 915 MHz, 2.45 GHz, and 5.8 GHz. The study found that the dielectric properties of adrenal tumours were influenced by the presence of lipid-rich adenomas, and the dielectric properties of Cushing's syndrome tumour were lowest in comparison to the tumours in patients diagnosed with Conn's syndrome and Pheochromocytoma. Furthermore, a notable difference was observed in the dielectric properties of the medulla and cortex among patients diagnosed with Conn's syndrome, Cushing's syndrome, and Pheochromocytoma.

record.abstract: We describe an algorithm that, given a postcritically finite quadratic polynomial, outputs a finite state machine whose regular language is the set of external arguments for all points on the Hubbard tree, generalizing an example of Milnor. record.abstract: The geometry of constraints in variational inequalities (VIs) plays a central role in applications ranging from resource allocation and equilibrium computation to constrained optimization. Yet, its effect on computational complexity has received surprisingly little attention beyond special cases. We examine this question when the constraint set is an $\ell_p$ ball. This family of problems encompasses two of the most extensively studied classes of problems in algorithmic game theory: symmetric bimatrix games for $p = 1$ and multi-player polymatrix games for $p = \infty$. Both of these problems are known to be PPAD-complete even for affine operators. We establish a comprehensive complexity landscape for VIs over $\ell_p$ balls across the full range $p\in[1,\infty]$. First, for any $p\neq 2$, we show that finding an inverse-polynomial approximate VI solution is PPAD-complete even for affine operators. In contrast, for $p=2$, we give a polynomial-time algorithm for affine VIs, extending a classic result of Ye (1992) beyond symmetric operators. On the other hand, once the operator becomes quadratic, we establish PPAD-completeness even at inverse polynomial precision. From a technical standpoint, we develop a new toolkit for exploiting the geometry of the constraint set and the structure of the operator to characterize the complexity of equilibrium and optimization problems, which is of independent interest.

record.abstract: Continuous glucose monitors, smartwatches, meal logs, and health profiles form a rich multimodal personal context that can significantly enhance glucose forecasting. However, existing methods struggle to effectively utilize these signals to improve glucose prediction because the relevance of different modalities varies drastically across individuals and time. We present GlucoAgent, an LLM-based agentic system that addresses this challenge through dynamic, case-by-case analysis at inference time. For each forecast, GlucoAgent writes and runs code over an individual's multimodal context and returns predictions with a reason and supporting evidence. The generated programs are highly diverse, ranging from retrieving similar past meals to fitting and back-testing physiological and statistical models. On CGMacros, a multimodal glucose dataset, GlucoAgent outperforms time series foundation models on every forecasting horizon, achieving an average RMSE of 22.5 mg/dL compared to 23.5 mg/dL of Chronos-2, the leading multimodal time series foundation model. Furthermore, GlucoAgent is highly effective at leveraging multimodal data. The addition of multimodal data reduces its average RMSE by 1.4 mg/dL (24.0 mg/dL to 22.5 mg/dL), compared to a marginal 0.3 mg/dL (23.8 mg/dL to 23.5 mg/dL) improvement for Chronos-2. This advantage is most pronounced in challenging post-meal windows, where GlucoAgent uses multimodal context to reduce 60-minute forecast RMSE by 4.6 mg/dL (31.0 mg/dL to 26.5 mg/dL), far exceeding the 0.8 mg/dL (31.9 mg/dL to 31.1 mg/dL) reduction achieved by Chronos-2.

record.abstract: NLP evaluation reports routinely cite sliced performance differences, most prominently the intra-inter gap in document-level relation extraction, as capability evidence. We show that such gap readings are joint properties of models and evaluation contracts: scoring function, gold version, threshold, output format, and prompt language. With predictions frozen, a method ordering reverses under a gold-standard exchange (+0.0363, CI excluding zero; tie-level after), movement localizing where gold re-partitions: renames are gauge transformations (Delta=0; re-annotation +0.862). We formalize this as an evaluation leverage account centered on the rank-flip condition. Constructively, the audited evaluation reading (AER) is a contract-marginalized, tie-declared, seed-prescribed, gate-filtered procedure whose tie declarations cover every contract-induced flip on the declared WMT19 grids (14/14; held-out 73% vs. union-of-ties 89%), matching the best single metric contract at epsilon=0.10 equivalence. Evidence spans DocRE, HacRED, a UD probe, and released gold revisions; an alternative-reference-set replication extends it beyond our testbeds. Failed predictions retained as boundaries; a 5% violation gate flags unverifiable settings and bounds survivor-selection bias. We release EvalLever, a preregistered workflow with an amendment trail; on LLM-as-judge grids, the audited ensemble stabilizes every unstable pair (13-15 to zero; generic ensemble shrinkage: the preregistered correlation criterion failed, the companion stabilization criterion passed).

record.abstract: Routing benchmarks often judge a router against a hindsight oracle that counts a query as solved whenever any model's recorded answer is correct, but under stochastic decoding that oracle mixes two different objects: the clairvoyant ceiling of committing to one model per query and the premium of calling several models and keeping any correct answer. A companion study measured this premium at 3.5 percentage points (pp) for 11 small open models on MATH-500; how large it is once current reasoning models enter the pool was unknown. We measure it with a fixed-protocol, pre-committed generation on a single NVIDIA B300: all 500 MATH-500 problems, 30 seeded samples per problem, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and NVIDIA's Nemotron Nano 9B v2 and Nemotron Super 49B v1.5 (a NAS derivative of the same 70B) under vendor sampling, a 65,536-token cap, a pinned Math-Verify scorer, and an append-only attempt ledger, for 45,000 scored responses. The two reasoning models both reach 96.1% accuracy against 76.2% for the 70B baseline. The empirical product-coupling premium is 0.215-0.588 pp across all two- and three-model pools; the empirical plug-in selection headroom over always calling Nano is 1.27 pp; and resampling Nano three times gives practically the same empirical any-correct rate as calling all three models once. Only 31 responses reached the cap, 25 of them with exactly periodic tails, yet the capped responses account for up to 60.2% of a model's output-length-squared proxy, and long generations made a fourth planned model, Llama-3.1-8B, too slow to finish. The premium is far below the companion's 3.5 pp, but models, pool size and protocol changed together; an oracle gap should therefore be reported with the pool, the protocol, the samples per cell and the decoding budget that produced it.

record.abstract: Optimizing accelerator code across hardware architectures is difficult. ML compilers search predefined spaces of schedules and micro-kernels, while LLM-guided optimization can explore alternative algorithms, operator decompositions, and hardware-specific techniques. However, existing LLM agents typically target a single programming interface, toolchain, or accelerator family, focus on kernel-level optimization without model-level transforms, and offer limited reuse of experience across hardware targets. We present ModelBlaster, a Memory-Augmented In-Context Reinforcement Learning (MAIC-RL) framework for optimizing data-parallel kernels and whole models across heterogeneous SIMD and SIMT accelerators. Its mutable policy is a persistent knowledge base updated at inference time by Actor-Critic Textual Gradient Descent (AC-TGD). The knowledge base maps performance states to actions, outcomes, and constraints, enabling experience reuse across kernels, models, and hardware targets. A model-level optimizer uses kernel-level knowledge to inform whole-model decisions. The same optimization loop and knowledge schema support CUDA on NVIDIA GPUs, OpenCL on Qualcomm GPUs, and RVV intrinsics on RISC-V vector cores, with only lowering and measurement layers specific to each target. Compared with PyTorch, ModelBlaster achieves geometric-mean speedups of 1.85x, 5.58x, and 5.18x on KernelBench Levels 1, 2, and 3, and 1.69x on SOL-ExecBench Levels 1 and 2 on a B200 GPU. On Qualcomm Adreno GPUs, it achieves 5.8x over the vendor SDK and 1.7x over Apache TVM; on RISC-V vector cores, it achieves 2.7x over ExecuTorch with XNNPACK across 70 KernelBench problems.

record.abstract: We study the optimal design of investment subsidies across heterogeneous monopolistic markets subject to a common expected discounted budget. Each producer faces a regular one-dimensional demand diffusion and chooses irreversible capacity expansion through a singular stochastic control problem. The regulator values weighted consumer surplus, producer profits, and an additional benefit from installed capacity, while accounting for the excess cost of raising public funds. We characterize producers' optimal investment responses through free boundaries and reformulate the regulator's stochastic optimization problem as a deterministic optimization over investment boundaries. An integral representation then recovers the optimal subsidy schedules that implement the resulting capacity policies. Under mild conditions on the diffusions, we establish existence of optimal schedules and uniqueness of the induced investment policies. Finally, we characterize the subsidy schedule and provide numerical illustrations.
